chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali died at Al-Abwa while he was in Ihram, and with him were Al-Hasan, Al-Husayn, and Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, and Abd Allah and Ubayd Allah, the two sons of al-Abbas. So they shrouded him, covered his face and head, and did not embalm him. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is how it is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)'.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْأَبْوَاء: Al-Abwa, a place between Mecca and Medina where the Prophet died
key_terms.كَفَّنُوهُ: They shrouded him (in the burial cloth)
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali, a reference to a specific juristic text or compilation attributed to Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What are the burial rulings for a person who dies while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the specific juristic ruling for a deceased pilgrim in Ihram, emphasizing the preservation of the state of consecration by covering the head and face while omitting full embalming (ta'thim). It links this practice directly to the 'Book of Ali' (Kitab Ali), reflecting the Shia tradition of attributing legal precedents to the Imam's personal codex or authoritative written record. The narration highlights the continuity of prophetic and imamic burial customs, distinguishing Ihram-specific rites from general funeral practices.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, having said:

‘Abdul Rahman Bin Al-Hassan Bin Ali died at Al-Abwa and he was in Ihraam, and with him were Al-Hassa, Al-Husayn, and Abdullah Bin Ja’far, and Abdullah, and Ubeydullah, the two sons of Al-Abbas. So they enshrouded him, and covered his face and his dead, and did not embalm him’. And heasws said: ‘This is how it is in the Book of Aliasws’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ibn Faddal from Yunus from Ya’qub from abu Maryam who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, died in al-Abwa’ (name of a place) in the state of Ihram. With him there were al-Hassan, al- Husayn, ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far, ‘Abd Allah and ‘Ubayd Allah sons of al-‘Abbas. They provided him shroud and covered his face and head, but did not use Hunut (rubbing camphor over the seven parts of the body which one places on the ground for Sajdah (prostration)) saying, ‘This is how it is written in the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’”
